[Pedagogy review · High priority · opening-review · pf-bdae8c3f35]
Before p3-formula-comparison add three short items: (a) For y=3x−4, find y when x=−1. Answer: −7. (b) For y=2^x−4, write the substituted expression and find y when x=0. Answer: 2^0−4=−3. (c) For y=3^(−x)−5, write the substituted expression and find y when x=−1. Answer: 3^(−(−1))−5=−2. Keep the review within one page.
Also affects: p5-example-right-node

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-5ff492d7ba]
After p8-q2-f add (g) Sketch y=3(2^x) and y=2^x+2 together, labelling their y-intercepts, horizontal asymptotes and points at x=1. Answer: both (0,3); respectively asymptotes y=0 and y=2, and points (1,6) and (1,4). (h) Explain why their shared y-intercept does not make them the same curve. Answer: their other plotted values and asymptotes differ.

[Pedagogy review · High priority · missing-prerequisite · pf-ba33583079]
The behaviour questions require approach notation that preceding teaching has not introduced.
Before p11-identify explain: 'x→∞ means move right without bound; x→−∞ means move left without bound. x→0+ means approach zero through positive values; x→0− means approach zero through negative values. For y, 0+ and 0− mean approach zero from above and below.' Model on y=1/x: 'As x→∞, y→0+; as x→0+, y→∞.'

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · variation-sequence · pf-aa32f4156d]
After p29-q3-i, under the existing sketching instruction, add only: 'Predict how many intercepts each circle has on each axis before sketching.' Add (j) (x−2)²+(y−4)²=1; (k) the same left side =4; (l) =9; (m) =16; (n) =25. Expected intercepts: j none; k only (0,4); l only (0,4±√5); m (2,0) and (0,4±2√3); n (−1,0), (5,0), (0,4±√21). Follow with unpatterned (o) (x+4)²+(y−1)²=9: centre (−4,1), x-intercepts (−4±2√2,0), no y-intercepts. In j–n only the radius varies; the centre remains (2,4).

[Pedagogy review · High priority · opening-review · pf-6aa838beee]
Before p32-key-idea add three short items: (a) Expand (x+3)² and (y−2)². Answers: x²+6x+9 and y²−4y+4. (b) Write x²+6x and y²−4y as a square minus a constant. Answers: (x+3)²−9 and (y−2)²−4. (c) Rearrange (x+3)²−9+(y−2)²−4−3=0 into centre-radius form. Answer: (x+3)²+(y−2)²=16. Include the reminder 'Halve the linear coefficient and square it; compensate for what you add.' In the example, identify 1=(2/2)² and 9=(−6/2)².
